notes.text:
Retain every smooth integral projective X of dimension n>=1 over every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, and every actual big rational L. Put theta=c1(L), K=X^an. FS stages are full finite section systems on actual rational bundles, may have common zeros, and use their canonical trivial reference. PSH(theta) means one all-point decreasing FS net on actual B_i with c1(B_i)->theta, having a finite generic endpoint. Supported semivaluations remain.

Only the complete caller G0 in its actual ample domain and G1 in its exact relative-generation/one-net domain are grants. Ordinary Kodaira decomposition, openness/numerical invariance of ampleness, ample generation and equivariant resolved model representation are scoped background. No unreviewed manuscript proposition is assumed here.

At each analytic valuation-ring center, a generating section is a unit. Thus the maximum of the canonical norms of a generating system is one at every point. Tensoring with this zero-weight system changes the actual bundle and preserves the scalar literally. Fix actual ample Omega with Omega-L ample. A tail of any defining net has Omega-B_i ample. Tensor into Omega and append generators with weight -mN: max(h_i,-N), directed in (i,N), is a single decreasing fixed-Omega net with endpoint u at every point. G0 therefore gives all-point order determination, generic-sup normalization, and uniform finite divisorial bounds for the whole normalized big cone inside one ample cone.

Finite maxima use valid triples of two incoming indices and epsilon>0 on actual L+epsilon A, with both actual ample differences. These triples are directed by decreasing epsilon and taking sufficiently late indices. Real convex combinations use rational coefficients r_j increasing to r and s_j increasing to 1-r, after shifting both inputs below a fixed finite C. The scalars r_j(h_i-C)+s_j(g_l-C)+C decrease; their actual tensor bundles tend to theta. Thus these are single nets, including at poles.

Choose an actual Kodaira identity L=aA+E0, a>0, A ample, E0 effective, W=log||s_E0||<=0, Z=E0^an. Given continuous bounded f and genuine u<=f, fix rational t in (0,1) and epsilon>0 before choosing an incoming tail. The bundle L-(1-t)B_i-t(L-aA) is eventually ample. The compact closed sets {h_i>=f+epsilon} decrease to empty, so a whole tail has h_i<f+epsilon on all K. Tensoring gives the actual L-FS minorant (1-t)(h_i-epsilon)+t(W-||f||). On K\Z let the incoming index tend to its endpoint, then t->0 and epsilon->0. Every genuine minorant is below the supremum Q_L(f) of actual L-FS minorants there.

For a rational model f, G1 supplies a single genuine endpoint Psi with Q_L(f)<=Psi<=f. The preceding inequality holds at all divisorial valuations. Both u and Psi already lie in the same ample cone, so G0 transfers order to every original point. Hence Psi is the genuine all-point P_theta(f). In particular R=P_theta(0) is genuine, R(v0)=0, and normalized u<=R<=0. For each actual big B, a fixed normalized late G1 reference stage psi_B on B+C/m satisfies R_B<=psi_B+c_B, for finite c_B. Separately normalized stages are not asserted to be decreasing.

Here is the flattening argument for decreasing u_i with finite generic endpoint u. A special actual FS stage on T_eta=L+eta A has data B=L+epsilon A, epsilon<eta/4, a normalized reference psi on S close to B, T_eta-S ample, a small rational delta>0 with T_eta-(1-delta)S ample, and inequalities F>=u+kappa and F>=(1-delta)psi-k. The guard kappa>0 is separate from the pole floor. Such stages exist by tensoring a late defining majorant of one u_i and this floor into T_eta, then taking their maximum.

For finitely many old special F_l, choose new eta below their epsilon_l and new S with B_l-S ample. Then psi<=R_B_l<=psi_l+c_l. Choose delta<all delta_l. A large k makes the new floor no larger than every old F_l, since its difference is at most (delta_l-delta)psi_l+(1-delta)c_l+k_l-k. At old poles the new floor is literally -infinity.

The compact comparison used to lower the other branch is valid across those poles: if F_l>=(1-delta_l)psi_l-k_l and h<=psi_l+C, assign h-F_l=-infinity where F_l=-infinity. Off poles its upper bound is delta_l psi_l+C+k_l, tending to -infinity at the pole; the comparison is usc. Decreasing comparisons with negative endpoint have an empty intersection of their nonnegative compact superlevels, hence an entire negative tail. All incoming u_i and sufficiently late stages of a fixed u_i satisfy the common bound h<=R_B_l+M+1<=psi_l+c_l+M+1, by embedding into actual B_l and generic normalization. Choose kappa<min kappa_l/4. Apply compact comparison first to u_i+2kappa, then to its literal stages h+kappa. One stage fits the new T_eta and satisfies h+kappa<=all old F_l. Its maximum with the new floor is a new special stage below them. Ordering all special stages by scalar and eta decrease gives one directed net whose classes tend to theta.

The infimum is exactly u at every point: for finite t>u(x), choose u_i(x)<t with margin, a late defining stage with h(x)+kappa<t, and k sufficiently large so the floor is below t at x. Directedness can subsequently impose any old constraints. This works for every finite t when u(x)=-infinity. Thus no twice-closed construction was assumed.

Every upper bounded usc obstacle with a genuine minorant is the infimum of a directed decreasing net of rational model majorants: continuous cutoffs supply majorants, uniform model approximation and finite minima retain the infimum. Their already genuine model envelopes decrease, have a finite generic lower bound, and the just-proved closure makes the endpoint genuine. It equals the raw envelope by order at every point. For S=sup u_alpha of any nonempty uniformly upper bounded family, P_theta(S*) is usc, dominates S, and is below S*. It consequently equals S* literally.

For compactness, embed a convergent normalized big-cone net in the compact normalized Omega cone. The tail regularizations S_i*=(sup_{j>=i}u_j)* are genuine big, decrease, and have generic value zero. Their genuine infimum b is in the big cone. The independently read BJ arXiv:1801.08229v4 Theorem 5.6/Lemma 5.7, applied only to Omega, gives S_i*(z)=sup_{j>=i}u_j(z) at every divisorial z: the proof supplies one continuous PL separator psi with sup(phi-psi) attained at z for every ample phi, and passes the uniform inequality to usc regularization. Thus b has the same divisorial coordinates as the ample limit, and G0 gives all-point equality. The normalized big cone is closed and compact. Rational divisorial scalings suffice: convex decreasing restrictions to each scaling ray and uniform ample bounds give equicontinuity on smaller intervals, so rational values determine real-scaled values and convergence.

notes.text:
Use the domain, genuine cone and scalar results of n1. A negligible subset is any D contained in the raw discrepancy {S<S*} for a nonempty uniformly upper bounded family in one numerical single-net cone. It need not be Borel. The following argument also works for a family in any fixed real numerical class for which this single-net cone is nonempty.

Choose one actual ample Omega whose numerical difference from the input class is ample. The tensor construction of n1 embeds every family member as the identical scalar at every original analytic point, including supported poles. Hence the raw S is identical in the two descriptions. S*(x)=inf over neighborhoods O of x of sup_{y in O}S(y) is identical too, since the topology and all values are unchanged. This is literal raw-supremum identification, not divisorial determination of a new supremum. For big-class families, n1 separately proves that S* itself is genuinely big psh.

Apply the primary BJ arXiv:1801.08229v4 Theorem 13.17 in the actual ample Omega class. X is irreducible and G0 supplies EP for Omega. The theorem proves that negligible sets are pluripolar: its Lemma 13.19 uses ample Choquet selection, quasicontinuity on a compact set and capacity comparison to show outer capacity zero; the Alexander--Taylor inequality and Theorem 4.45 then give an Omega-psh pole. It is not a definitional identification of negligible with polar. Choose this p with p(v0)=0 and p=-infinity on D. The pertinent primary theorem and proof, including Lemma 13.19, were independently retrieved/read at renderer 10614--10647, saved local LF1--34. Ancillary complete proof units for polar detection, Choquet, capacity/quasicontinuity/comparison, and outer capacity are recorded in the source ledger. No big capacity theorem is applied.

Since L is big, choose rational t>0 with L-tOmega big. A nonzero section of a cleared positive multiple supplies an effective rational divisor E and an actual bundle identity L=tOmega+E. Take the fixed actual Omega decreasing FS net p_i from G0. Clearing powers and tensoring its sections with s_E gives actual L-FS scalars q_i=t p_i+log||s_E||. They form one decreasing net. At zeros of s_E every stage and the endpoint are -infinity; elsewhere the endpoint is tp+log||s_E||. Its generic value is finite and its pole contains D. Thus every such negligible set is covered by one genuine big-class psh pole on the original carrier. Conversely each genuine big pole is an ample pole by the same scalar embedding. This proves pole-covering equivalence, not finite-energy membership or measure nullness.

The additional E1 step has explicit, still unproved hypotheses here: whole genuine scalar energy E is concave, monotone and decreasing continuous, E(R)=0, E(u+c)=E(u)+cV for V=vol(L)>0, and B((1-r)R+ru)<=C r^2 B(u) for every normalized genuine finite-energy u, where B=-E. Do not use this implication to establish those inputs.

Under these hypotheses normalize a genuine pole q. Let N_j=16^j, r_j=8^-j and lambda_j=2^-j. Genuine truncations q_j=max(q,R-N_j) satisfy B(q_j)<=VN_j. Set a_j=(1-r_j)R+r_j q_j, so B(a_j)<=CV4^-j. The actual convex sums p_m=sum_{j<=m}lambda_j a_j+2^-mR decrease, have generic value zero, and E(p_m)>=-CV sum 8^-j>=-CV/7. The closure proved in n1 supplies a genuine endpoint; the assumed decreasing energy continuity makes it E1. Where q=-infinity and R finite, the exact relative sum R-p_m=sum_{j<=m}lambda_j r_j N_j=m. Its endpoint p is therefore a finite-energy pole covering that part of the q pole.

Any finite positive Radon measure missing {R=-infinity} and integrating EVERY genuine relative E1 test has zero measure on the Borel infinite-cost set of this p. It has a Borel null superset of D, so D has outer measure zero even if D itself is not Borel. This covers nonalgebraic discrepancies conditionally. notes.detailedSummary: On a finite common nef model, the mixed raw measure is 1/n! times the alternating sum of |S|^n times the diagonal measure at the average of slots indexed by S. The proof is all-dimension monomial cancellation. Convergence and independence follow only if every such actual rational-barycenter diagonal limit is independently identified; this has not been proved. The exact program exhausts 637 monomials in dimensions 1--6 and checks raw mass coefficients. On Bl_p P2, vol(H+aE)=1 for a>=0 and 1-a^2 for -1<a<0, proved from sections. Thus ordinary big volume is not a single polynomial even on this entirely big segment and cannot replace the missing mixed-operator identification.
notes.text:
For n finite nef slots T_1,...,T_n on one common determination, with the same generic bundle, the raw component coefficient at v_E is b_E times the product of their restrictions to E. Every b_E is retained. Finite nef interpretation can be obtained by adding the same zero ample epsilon H to the generic slots, applying the actual ample finite G0 formula, and taking the finite polynomial limit epsilon->0. This imports no unbounded nonample assertion.

Multilinearity gives the exact raw formula
mu(T_1,...,T_n) = (1/n!) sum over nonempty S subset {1,...,n} of (-1)^(n-|S|) |S|^n MA_raw((sum_{i in S} T_i)/|S|).
To prove it, expand degree-n monomials. Every monomial missing an index cancels in the alternating sum over its supersets. The only monomial involving all n indices has all powers one and coefficient n!. This proves the identity for all dimensions, with no division by volume. In dimension two it is 2 MA_raw((u1+u2)/2) - (MA_raw(u1)+MA_raw(u2))/2.

Conditional consequence: if a shared moving approximant family has the correct diagonal weak limits at each of these finitely many rational barycenters, the mixed measures converge weakly to the displayed finite sum of endpoint outputs. Positivity follows because every finite mixed measure is positive; the constant continuous test gives the raw limiting mass; independence holds between families satisfying precisely this hypothesis. No unbounded test is passed. Genuine endpoint convex combinations are available by n1, but their moving raw diagonal compatibility is not supplied by n1.

The unresolved input cannot be replaced by convergence for endpoints and maxima alone. A maximum uses a union in one degree. A rational convex combination uses tensor products in a larger degree, where the complete moving horizontal factor may change. The fixed-factor energy squeeze and full-section lost-rank defect must be justified again. Neither the required barycenter convergence nor the later simultaneous unbounded weighted independence is proved here.

An independent algebraic diagnostic is explicit. On Bl_p P2 write H for the pulled hyperplane and E for the exceptional curve. For rational -1<a<1 and cleared degree m, when a>=0 the negative intersection with E forces maE into every divisor; stripping it identifies H0(m(H+aE)) with H0(mH). When a=-b<0, sections are degree-m polynomials vanishing to order mb at p. At p=[1:0:0], homogeneous monomials x0^(m-i-j)x1^i x2^j with i+j<mb give exactly binom(mb+1,2) independent conditions. Thus h0 is binom(m+2,2) on a>=0 and binom(m+2,2)-binom(mb+1,2) on a<0. Dividing by m^2/2 gives volume 1 and 1-a^2, respectively. All these bundles are big. A polynomial constant on an open half-interval is constant everywhere, contradicting the negative side. A quadratic interpolation through a=-1/2,0,1/2 gives 1+a/4-a^2/2. At a=1/4 its value is 33/32, whereas the proved volume is 1. This rejects ordinary-volume polynomial interpolation as an automatic mixed operator, not a valid same-class analytic construction.

notes.text:
Retain the same smooth integral projective X, n>=1, and fields, but let actual rational L be numerically trivial, including nontorsion Pic0. Use the literal varying-actual-bundle single-net cone at numerical class zero and zero reference.

For rational epsilon>0, actual L+epsilon A is ample. A zero-weight generating system has scalar zero at every point. These constants on classes tending to zero give one defining net, and shifts give every real constant. Conversely normalize u in PSH(0) at v0 to zero. Integer tensoring gives mu in PSH(0) for every positive integer m. Fix one actual ample Omega. For each m the scalar mu embeds into Omega by the same elementary actual ample difference tensoring and generator floors: a defining class tending to zero eventually has ample difference to Omega. All these normalized mu lie in its one compact normalized ample cone. A fixed divisorial coordinate has a finite uniform bound -C_z<=mu(z)<=0. Let m->infinity to get u(z)=0. The all-point order determination in G0 gives u=0 at every original point, including supported points. Thus PSH(0)=R independently of big energy.

On this entire classified cone define the raw zero-class operator and raw energy by the constant ample perturbations. Their top masses are epsilon^n(A^n)->0 and their constant energies are c epsilon^n(A^n)->0. Positivity makes every continuous test integral tend to zero. Hence MA_raw(c)=0, E_raw(c)=0, E1(0)=R. The only positive mass-zero Radon target is literally the zero measure; the equation is attained, and all its solutions differ by constants. Its zero dual energy, comparison and both zero derivative signs follow directly. No mass is probability-normalized.

This range does not cover all zero-volume pseudoeffective data. On P1 x P1, take the nonzero nef L=p1*O(1). Pull back the global generated-system FS scalar from two homogeneous coordinates weighted 0,-1. It is bounded, nonconstant, and differs from zero by more than a constant. Add the zero metric on epsilon O(1,1). Both actual ample bundles have top mass 2epsilon(1+epsilon)->0; positivity therefore forces both raw top limits to be zero. The whole bounded cone with this raw equation has at least two distinct solutions modulo constants. A wider uniqueness assertion needs a replacement datum. This is not a counterexample to the positive-volume equation and is not a complete solution of original P16.5.
